technical_and_design_decisions: Fix U1 by initializing a default Sqoop connection manager when an explicit JDBC driver is supplied, preventing the NPE, rather than forcing use of the Hortonworks Teradata connector.
Make the log directory configurable via a new property `xd.log.dir` (default `${xd.home}/logs`), consumed by the logging framework at startup; RPM packaging sets it to `/var/log/spring-xd`.
Extract message-bus and serialization codec into a separate `spring-bus` Maven artifact, exposing the same public APIs so Spring XD can depend on it.
Move input/output type conversion into `spring-cloud-dataflow` to enable reuse by custom modules, defining a clear conversion SPI.
Implement the single-node Admin SPI (`SingleNodeAdmin`) using the existing `ModuleLauncher` to deploy modules inside one JVM with a shared parent context.
Implement the Diego Admin SPI (`DiegoAdmin`) via a REST client to the Diego Receptor API, reusing `ModuleLauncher` for module packaging and lifecycle.
For U8, base the investigation on Spring Cloud `DiscoveryClient` (e.g., Eureka/Consul) to allow modules to self-register and XD to discover them.
Maintain backward compatibility: default behaviors, stream/job definitions, and existing configurations remain unchanged after refactors.
Use Maven for builds, semantic versioning, and publish snapshot artifacts to an internal repository for integration.
assumptions: A single developer with working knowledge of Spring XD, Sqoop, and Spring Cloud performs all tasks.
A Teradata test instance (or Teradata Express VM) and the official Teradata JDBC driver are available for testing U1.
The `spring-bus` and `spring-cloud-dataflow` repositories exist or can be created with appropriate write access.
Baseline Spring XD version already contains the `ModuleLauncher` and Admin SPI abstractions required by U6/U7.
For U7, a local Lattice/Diego environment or a mock Receptor HTTP server is available for testing; otherwise tests use mocks.
U8 is treated as a research spike: deliver a prototype and recommendation, not a production-ready feature.
Effort estimates cover analysis, coding, unit/integration testing, and documentation, but exclude end-user training, production deployment, and ongoing maintenance.
All estimates are expressed in work-hours for one developer; no parallelization or calendar constraints are considered.
If minor legacy obstacles are encountered, they are absorbed within the most-likely estimates.
